Intro

Du möchtest an einer Legal-Tech-Anwendung arbeiten, die für E-Commerce-Unternehmen wie eine digitale Rechtsabteilung funktioniert? Du denkst Systeme vom Datenmodell bis zur Oberfläche, konzipierst gern technische Lösungen und übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, dass sie am Ende auch so umgesetzt werden? Dann bist du als Senior Fullstack-Entwickler (m/w/d) / Senior Webentwickler PHP/Laravel (m/w/d) beim Händlerbund genau richtig!

Bei uns entwickelst du an einer Plattform, die rechtliche Prozesse digital abbildet und automatisiert. Von der Erstellung rechtlicher Inhalte über Vertrags- und Prüfprozesse bis hin zu Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsfragen. Dazu gehören Schnittstellen und Plugins, über die unsere Inhalte in die Shopsysteme unserer Mitglieder gelangen, sowie Integrationen mit Partnersystemen. Ziel ist es, komplexe rechtliche Anforderungen in verlässliche, verständliche und effiziente digitale Workflows zu überführen.

In dieser Rolle übernimmst du die technische Leitung von Projekten, die wir in kleinen Projektteams umsetzen: Du konzipierst Lösungen, verantwortest die Umsetzung, leitest andere Entwickler im Projekt an und hältst alle Beteiligten über den Stand auf dem Laufenden. Kleinere Projekte setzt du eigenständig komplett um, bei größeren arbeitest du im Team mit Laravel und Livewire im Stack.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Technische Konzeption: Analyse von Anforderungen, Entwurf der Lösungsarchitektur, Festlegung von Datenmodellen und Schnittstellen sowie Einschätzung von Aufwänden für Features und Projekte.

  • Ownership für die Umsetzung: Verantwortung dafür, dass ein Projekt von der Konzeption bis zum Go-live ankommt. Aufgaben schneiden und priorisieren, Fortschritt im Blick behalten, technische Entscheidungen treffen und Blocker aus dem Weg räumen.

  • Anleitung & Wissenstransfer: Fachliche Führung weiterer Entwickler im Projekt durch klare technische Vorgaben, Pairing und Code Reviews im Backend wie im Frontend. Wissen über Architektur und Entscheidungen landet im Team und in der Dokumentation, nicht nur bei dir.

  • Reporting: Regelmäßige, verständliche Berichte zu Stand, Risiken und nächsten Schritten an Team Lead, Product Owner und Stakeholder.

  • Fullstack-Entwicklung: Umsetzung mit Laravel, Livewire, Alpine.js, Flux UI und Tailwind CSS. Kleinere Projekte eigenständig von Anfang bis Ende, größere im Projektteam.

  • Partneranbindungen & Integrationen: Lösungsevaluierung, Umsetzung und Dokumentation von Schnittstellen zu Partner- und Drittsystemen.

  • Architektur & Technologie-Evaluation: Mitgestaltung von Architektur, Entwicklungsstandards und Tooling; Evaluation neuer Technologien, Frameworks und KI-Einsatzmöglichkeiten im Hinblick auf ihren konkreten Nutzen für Produkt und Team.


Dein Profil

Technisch

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit PHP & Laravel: Entwicklung von Webanwendungen über den gesamten Stack, im Frontend idealerweise mit Livewire, Alpine.js, Flux UI und Tailwind CSS.

  • Konzeption & technische Leitung: Erfahrung darin, technische Konzepte zu erarbeiten und deren Umsetzung zu verantworten, allein oder als technische Leitung eines Projektteams.

  • Code Reviews über den gesamten Stack: Praxis im Review von Backend- und Frontend-Code und die Fähigkeit, Feedback so zu geben, dass andere daran wachsen.

  • Testerfahrung: Sicherer Umgang mit PHPUnit oder Pest und Erfahrung mit Teststrategien in größeren Codebasen. Tests sind für dich Teil der Umsetzung, nicht Nacharbeit.

  • Datenbanken & APIs: Sicherer Umgang mit relationalen Datenbanken, Datenmodellierung und API-Design.

  • Agile Teamarbeit: Erfahrung in agilen Teams, idealerweise mit Scrum, inklusive enger Zusammenarbeit und kontinuierlichem Austausch.


Nice to Have, aber kein Muss

  • DevOps-Erfahrung: Cloud-Systeme, PaaS-Plattformen, Container, CI/CD oder Linux-Serveradministration (z.B. DigitalOcean und Laravel Cloud)

  • Erfahrung mit Shopsystemen und der Entwicklung von Plugins oder Apps dafür (z.B. Shopify oder JTL)

  • Gespür für UX und Erfahrung in der Gestaltung benutzerfreundlicher Oberflächen

  • Erfahrung mit Event-basierten Architekturen, Queues oder asynchronen Verarbeitungsprozessen

  • Erfahrung mit der Integration von LLM-APIs in Produktfeatures (Prompting, Evaluierung, Guardrails)


Persönlich

jobs.description:
About Passionfroot

Creator-led growth is one of the fastest-growing channels in B2B—and we’re building the infrastructure behind it.

Passionfroot is the leading platform where modern companies scale creator-led growth, and where top creators manage and monetize brand partnerships.

Our customers include some of the most ambitious, fastest-moving companies in the world—Replit, HubSpot, Figma, Cursor, Gamma, Attio, Intercom, and ElevenLabs. We help them run high-impact creator programs across LinkedIn, YouTube, newsletters, and more.

We're growing 13x in revenue year over year, profitable, and just closed our Series A round! We are backed by leading investors including Insight Partners, Creandum, Supernode and founders and operators from Cursor, Anthropic, n8n and more. We're expanding fast across New York, Europe, and Brazil - and we're just getting started.

We’re still a small team, which means the people who join now will have an outsized influence on the product, the engineering culture, and the company we become.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior or Staff Product Engineer to help build the next generation of Passionfroot.

You’ll work across the full stack on both our core platform and Zest, our AI Campaign Manager for creator marketing. That could mean designing a new workflow for managing creator campaigns, making collaboration data feel instant, or turning models, search, and product context into a reliable AI experience that customers can trust.

We don’t separate “AI engineering” from “product engineering.” AI is becoming part of how the product works, but great product fundamentals still matter: understanding the user, shaping the problem, choosing the right architecture, building a thoughtful experience, and operating it reliably in production.

You’ll work closely with the founders, design, and customers to take important problems from early exploration to shipped product.

We’re a team of six engineers, and staying small is deliberate. It means you can have an idea on Monday and have customers using it by Thursday—without layers of sprint ceremonies or alignment meetings in between. The flip side is real ownership: you need to exercise strong judgment, communicate your decisions, and think through their consequences rather than wait for someone else to catch them.

📍This role is based in our Berlin or São Paulo offices with a hybrid work model. We are also open to candidates who are willing to relocate to either area.

What you’ll do

  • Own meaningful product areas from problem definition through architecture, implementation, launch, and iteration.

  • Build customer-facing features across our marketplace, campaign management, collaboration, payments, analytics, and creator workflows.

  • Help make Zest an indispensable part of how modern companies run creator-led growth.

  • Turn foundation models into structured, reliable product experiences—not just impressive prototypes.

  • Work on intelligent workflows involving agents, tools, retrieval, search, recommendations, and generated interfaces.

  • Develop the evaluations, observability, and feedback loops needed to understand whether AI features are genuinely useful.

  • Work closely with design to create experiences that are fast, intuitive, and polished.

  • Talk directly with customers and translate ambiguous needs into simple product decisions.

  • Make pragmatic architectural choices that balance speed, quality, maintainability, and performance.

  • Improve the systems and engineering practices that help a small team ship reliably at high velocity.

  • At Staff level, provide technical direction across projects, raise the engineering bar, and help other engineers make better decisions.

What we’re looking for

  • Significant experience building and shipping high-quality, customer-facing software. 5+ years is a useful guide, but the scope and quality of your work matter more than the number.

  • Strong TypeScript and React fundamentals, with experience working across the full stack.

  • A track record of independently driving complex features or products from an ambiguous starting point to measurable customer impact. When you encounter a blocker, you investigate, communicate, and find another path forward without waiting to be managed.

  • Strong product and technical judgment. You care about what should be built, how it should feel, and whether it actually solves the problem. You can distinguish between problems that need a sophisticated system and problems that need a simple, well-executed solution.

  • Experience building with LLMs or other applied AI systems in production.

  • An understanding of the challenges behind reliable AI products: evaluation, context, retrieval, model behavior, latency, cost, observability, and failure modes.

  • Clear, proactive communication and the ability to collaborate effectively in a remote environment.

  • Care for software craftsmanship without losing sight of momentum and customer outcomes.

Our technology

Passionfroot is built primarily in TypeScript across the full stack.

Our core product uses React, Remix, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Zero sync for real-time product experiences. Our AI systems use foundation models from multiple providers alongside the AI SDK, Typesense, and Laminar for search, agent workflows, evaluations, and observability.

You don’t need experience with everything we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, relevant product experience, and your ability to learn quickly.

What success looks like

Within your first months, you will have:

  • Developed a deep understanding of creator-led growth and the problems our customers face.

  • Taken ownership of a major product or technical area with limited oversight.

  • Improved how we build, evaluate, and operate AI-powered functionality.

  • Earned the trust of the team through reliable execution and clear communication.

  • Helped us make better product and technical decisions beyond your immediate projects.

Our interview process

We want the process to be useful, respectful, and representative of how we actually work. We don’t use take-home challenges or algorithmic whiteboard interviews.

The process typically includes:

  1. A short introductory call.

  2. A conversation with Lorenzo about your experience, ambitions, and the work you are most proud of.

  3. A technical walkthrough of a project you know deeply, focused on the decisions and trade-offs you made.

  4. A collaborative product and technical problem-solving session with members of the team.

  5. A paid work trial based on a realistic problem, which can be completed flexibly around your current commitments.

  6. References and offer.

We aim to complete the process within one to two weeks.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and equity in a Series A company.

  • Remote-first work with the option to work together in Berlin if you are local.

  • Latest Apple hardware and the tools you need to do your best work.

  • 25 days of paid vacation, plus local public holidays.

  • Regular team events and off-sites—past destinations include Mallorca, Barcelona, the South of France, Berlin, and the Baltic Sea.

jobs.description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

About the role

As a Senior Frontend Engineer on our Website team, you'll be a co-owner of the platform behind synthesia.io: the component library, content model and rendering stack that every page on our marketing site is built from. You'll shape direction and make key technical decisions with the team, likely with a focus area of your own but context across the whole system. This is a hands-on engineering role, and your primary output is high-quality component and schema code, plus the tooling that lets others build with it.

Millions of people visit synthesia.io every month, and it is one of the main ways we win new customers. That comes with real responsibility. The decisions you make are seen at scale, and we set the quality bar accordingly.

The defining challenge of this role is composability: a marketing site that marketers, and increasingly AI agents, can build pages with, without breaking design, performance or SEO.

You can expect to:

  • Build, scale and evolve our section library: the Astro components, Sanity schemas and design tokens that let us compose marketing pages consistently and accessibly.

  • Own the content model. Design schemas that resist misuse, so an editor, or an agent, can build a page that is correct by construction rather than correct by review.

  • Take Figma component specs all the way to production: responsive across mobile, tablet and desktop, accessible by default, matching design intent precisely.

  • Extend the platform for AI-assisted development, so coding agents can generate on-brand, on-spec sections from a design spec as reliably as a person can.

  • Own SEO integrity as a first-class engineering concern: canonicals, sitemaps, structured data, redirects, and no traffic cliffs on launch.

  • Raise the bar on engineering standards across the website surface: thorough code review, patterns others can follow, and tests around the parts that actually break.

  • Maintain and extend localisation across nine locales and a translation pipeline, so the system works for a global audience.

  • Shape the technical direction of the website platform over the next 6 to 12 months, and champion its adoption with the people who publish on it.

What we're looking for

  • At least five (5) years as a software engineer, including three (3) at senior level, building front end for content-driven or marketing platforms.

  • Real ownership of a content model in Sanity. You've designed schemas other people had to live with, and you have opinions about references vs. embedded objects, when a variant belongs in the schema versus at runtime, and how to stop a section library sprawling. GROQ and Portable Text are familiar territory.

  • Deep front-end expertise: expert HTML, CSS and TypeScript, with a strong command of component API design and the developer experience of a shared library.

  • You can work end to end. Comfortable owning the server side as well as the front end: SSR, serverless and edge runtimes, API routes, a SQL database, secrets and CI. You should be able to take a feature from schema to component to the route that serves it without handing off, and be happy debugging something that only reproduces in production.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility and web performance, and comfortable building to WCAG 2.2 AA. Accessibility is part of your definition of done, not a separate pass.

  • You care that marketing sites are measured, on performance, SEO, analytics events and conversion, and you're happy being accountable to those numbers.

  • A strong sense of craft and attention to detail, and the judgement to balance design intent against engineering constraints.

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills. You explain your reasoning, review generously, and treat levelling up the people around you as part of the job.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience working on a large SaaS marketing website, at real traffic and with real stakes attached.

  • Astro, or another islands or static-site framework.

  • Cloudflare Workers, or another edge or serverless platform.

  • Experience with AWS Lambda.

  • Tailwind CSS v4, and experience working from a token-based design system.

  • Experience, or strong interest, in making component libraries and content models consumable by AI agents.

  • A strong design sensibility: an eye for visual detail and the judgement to push back on and improve design decisions, not just build them.

  • Experience with localisation and internationalisation at scale for a global audience.

  • Analytics and tag management implementation: dataLayer events, server-side tagging, getting attribution right without hurting performance.

Our culture

At Synthesia we're passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.

The hiring process:

  • 30 min call with our Technical Recruiter

  • 45 min call with the Head of Website about your past projects

  • 75 min practical exercise with one of our engineers. We hand you a real Figma section spec and work through how you'd model and build it. Collaborative, not Leetcode.

jobs.title: Stage - Contrôle de Gestion & Data / Performance (H/F)
jobs.description:
Chez Withings, nous souhaitons redonner aux individus le contrôle de leur santé.

Nous avons l’obsession de créer des produits beaux et intuitifs, afin que chacun puisse les utiliser facilement au quotidien; nos balances connectées, montres hybrides, tensiomètres, moniteurs de sommeil et tous les dispositifs de notre gamme sont aujourd’hui utilisés par des millions d’utilisateurs.

Notre objectif : permettre la prévention, le dépistage et l’accompagnement d’un certain nombre de maladies chroniques via des produits et des services innovants, afin de révolutionner la manière dont on prend soin de notre santé.

Rattaché(e) au Responsable Contrôle de Gestion, vous serez au cœur du pilotage de la performance et de la structuration de la donnée financière. Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes opérationnelles et la finance : analyser, fiabiliser et automatiser l'information pour aider les équipes à décider vite et bien, sur la performance commerciale comme sur les dépenses d'exploitation.

Au-delà du contrôle de gestion classique, vous contribuerez directement à nos chantiers data : construction d'une base CA/Marge unifiée et automatisation des reportings récurrents. Un vrai terrain de jeu pour un profil qui aime croiser finance et outils.

Missions

1. Analyse de la performance commerciale et du forecast

  • Assurer l'analyse hebdomadaire des installations, du sell-out et des stocks distributeurs.
  • Mettre à jour ces données dans notre outil de planification Anaplan et alerter sur les principales variations.
  • Participer aux revues mensuelles de forecast avec les équipes commerciales pour analyser la cohérence et les écarts au budget.

2. Suivi de la performance opérationnelle et des OPEX

  • Aider l'équipe finance à déployer le suivi des dépenses d'exploitation (OPEX) par service.
  • Analyser et présenter les suivis OPEX aux responsables budgétaires, avec un vrai rôle d'alerte sur les dérives.

3. Automatisation et fiabilisation du reporting

  • Contribuer à la construction et à la fiabilisation de notre base de données CA/Marge (réconciliation multi-sources SAP et e-commerce).
  • Automatiser des reportings récurrents (Net Margin, OPEX, Flash Finance) via requêtes et outils dédiés.
  • Participer aux analyses liées aux nouveaux flux : migration Shopify, partenariats B2B et nouveaux projets d'intégration.

4. Gestion des outils et analyses ad-hoc

  • Assurer la collecte, la mise à jour et la fiabilité des données dans nos outils de pilotage.
  • Réaliser des analyses ponctuelles pour les autres services : prévisions d'installations pour le service client, estimation des volumes des nouveaux produits, etc.

Requirements

  • Étudiant(e) en école de commerce, d'ingénieur ou cursus finance / data, en césure ou en fin d'études, avec une première approche du contrôle de gestion et un vrai intérêt pour la donnée.
  • Excellente maîtrise d'Excel : formules avancées, TCD, modélisation.
  • Appétence forte pour la data et l'automatisation. Des notions de SQL et / ou Python sont un vrai plus et pourront être développées pendant le stage.
  • La connaissance d'Anaplan et/ou SAP est un atout.
  • Organisé(e) et rigoureux(se), vous gérez plusieurs sujets en parallèle.
  • Autonome et curieux(se), vous prenez des initiatives et apprenez vite.
  • Excellent(e) communicant(e), vous aimez le travail en équipe et savez interagir avec des interlocuteurs variés.
  • Vous parlez couramment anglais.

Benefits

Rejoindre l’aventure Withings, c’est :

  • Intégrer un des pionniers et leaders mondiaux de la santé connectée, plusieurs fois primé au Consumer Electronic Show
  • Contribuer à des projets innovants et ambitieux pour la santé de demain dans un environnement agile et en constante évolution
  • Intégrer une entreprise internationale, membre de la FrenchTech 120, dont les équipes sont basées à Issy-les-Moulineaux, Boston, Hong-Kong et Shenzhen
  • Participer à l’amélioration continue de nos produits et services en les bêta-testant avant leur sortie, notamment lors de nos nombreuses sessions sportives entre collègues
  • Bénéficier de nombreux avantages : Stock Options, smartphone et ordinateur de votre choix, réductions pour des activités culturelles et sportives, restaurant d’entreprise, et bien plus encore
  • Collaborer avec des collègues passionnés et célébrer ensemble chacune de nos réussites !

Toutes les candidatures reçues sont étudiées indépendamment de l’origine ethnique, des opinions, des croyances, de la religion, du genre, de l’orientation sexuelle ou de la santé des candidats. Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

THE ROLE

The Transaction Monitoring (TM) Compliance Manager is a specialized financial crime risk and regulatory oversight role within the Second Line of Defence (2LoD) Financial Crime Compliance department. The successful candidate is responsible for providing independent oversight, objective evaluation, and compliance challenges regarding the efficacy of the firm's Transaction Monitoring framework.

Acting as a Second Line Subject Matter Expert (SME), the individual defines the regulatory envelope, assesses TM risk coverage, and reviews the governance, methodologies, and documentation underpinning detection mechanisms. This role does not own control execution or technical solution design; instead, it provides independent assurance to ensure that the firm’s monitoring practices remain aligned with defined risk appetite, internal policies, and global regulatory expectations (AML/CTF/CPF).


Key Responsibilities:


1. Compliance Oversight in Risk Assessment & Horizon Scanning

  • Independent Review: Lead the ongoing 2LoD evaluation and challenge of the Compliance Risk Assessments (including EWRA and Product Risk Assessments) to ensure they accurately reflect current transaction data, typologies, and product utilization trends.

  • Regulatory Surveying & Horizon Scanning: Proactively monitor, survey, and analyze shifts in the global regulatory landscape, financial crime trends, and regulatory enforcement actions to ensure the firm's TM Compliance risk assessment framework remains comprehensive and defensible.

  • Gap Assurance: Evaluate the mapping of financial crime typologies against active transaction monitoring coverage to independently identify and escalate potential tracking gaps to senior management.

2. Independent Compliance Challenge & Assurance Framework

  • Segmentation & Calibration Challenge: Provide independent, 2LoD challenge to data-driven customer segmentation methodologies executed by the First Line (1LoD), verifying alignment with merchant risk profiles.

  • Compliance Oversight in Tuning & Optimization: Review and evaluate the methodologies, statistical testing parameters, and documentation for periodic "Below-the-Line" (BTL) and "Above-the-Line" (ATL) testing performed by the First Line to ensure robust governance.

  • Residual Risk Opining: Formulate independent compliance opinions regarding residual risk acceptance, providing formal advisory input to governance forums and the Global MLROs.

3. Governance, Risk, & Reporting

  • Model Risk Governance: Participate in the compliance review of TM systems and model validation exercises, independently assessing the transparency, logic, and regulatory defensibility of detection models against applicable guidance (e.g., FCA guidance on model risk management).

  • Strategic Alignment: Provide regulatory compliance support to the Head of TM to assist in aligning roadmap initiatives with the compliance maturity framework.

  • Stakeholder Engagement: Engage with cross-functional stakeholders across lines of defense to communicate compliance requirements and support the adherence to established TM standards.

  • Governance & Escalation Paths: Support the enhancement of the TM compliance governance framework to facilitate the structured, independent escalation of risk metrics to senior management.

  • Metrics & KRI Oversight: Assist in the production of 2LoD Management Information (MI) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to track the effectiveness of the compliance oversight posture for the Head of TM and Global MLRO.

3. Data Integrity & Alert Lifecycle Assurance

  • Data Lineage Assurance: Review documentation regarding data lineage, integrity, and completeness for feeds ingested into the monitoring architecture to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.

  • Lifecycle Evaluation: Evaluate the end-to-end alert workflow governance, risk scoring frameworks, and prioritization mechanics to ensure high-risk alerts adhere to compliant escalation paths.

  • Feedback Loops: Analyze high-level alert outcomes and disposition trends to provide compliance feedback loops to technical teams, supporting iterative improvements in the quality of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs).

Qualifications & Experience

  • Experience: Typically 5+ years of experience within Financial Crime Compliance, with a specific focus on the independent oversight, assurance, or evaluation of Transaction Monitoring frameworks within a regulated PSP, FinTech, or financial institution.

  • 2LoD Competency: Proven experience operating within a Second Line of Defence capacity, demonstrating the ability to independently challenge technical teams, data models, and threshold tuning documentation objectively.

  • Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of the UK Money Laundering Regulations (MLRs), JMLSG Guidance, and international FATF standards.

  • Systems & Data Literacy: Familiarity with data analysis methodologies, data visualization tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau), or basic query languages (e.g., SQL) sufficient to independently evaluate data testing outputs, methodologies, and audit trails.

  • Education & Professional Certifications: A Bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Criminology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Professional certifications from recognized bodies (e.g., ICA International Diploma in AML, ACAMS) are highly regarded.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com, follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram

jobs.description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the only unified payments and financial platform for global businesses. Powered by our unique combination of proprietary infrastructure and software, we empower over 250,000 businesses worldwide – including Brex, Navan, Qantas, SHEIN and many more – with fully integrated solutions to manage everything from business accounts, payments, spend management and treasury, to embedded finance at a global scale.

Proudly founded in Melbourne, we have a team of over 2,300 of the brightest and most innovative people in tech across 27 offices around the globe. Valued at US$11 billion and backed by world-leading investors including T. Rowe Price, Visa, Mastercard, Robinhood Ventures, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures, DST Global, and Lone Pine Capital, Airwallex is leading the charge in building the global payments and financial platform of the future. If you’re ready to do the most ambitious work of your career, join us.

 

Attributes We Value

We hire successful builders with founder-like energy who want real impact, accelerated learning, and true ownership. You bring strong role-related expertise and sharp thinking, and you’re motivated by our mission and operating principles. You move fast with good judgment, dig deep with curiosity, and make decisions from first principles, balancing speed and rigor.

You're humble and collaborative; turn zero‑to‑one ideas into real products, and you “get stuff done” end-to-end. You use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster. Here, you’ll tackle complex, high‑visibility problems with exceptional teammates and grow your career as we build the future of global banking. If that sounds like you, let’s build what’s next.

 

What you’ll do

As Associate Corporate Counsel, you will support Airwallex’s growth in the UK by providing practical, business-focused legal advice on corporate, regulatory and commercial matters. You will work closely with Corporate Development on strategic transactions such as fundraising and M&A, partner with UK and regional leaders on new market entry, support license expansion, and help align Airwallex’s global policies and governance with UK and relevant EMEA requirements. You will also advise on marketing, referral and partnership initiatives, ensuring go-to-market activity is compliant and enables ambitious but responsible growth. This role is based in London.

Responsibilities

You will:

  • Provide clear, pragmatic advice on UK and relevant EMEA legal and regulatory requirements impacting Airwallex entities in the region, helping teams navigate applicable rules while enabling responsible growth.

  • Support Corporate Development on fundraising rounds and strategic transactions, including due diligence, data rooms, corporate approvals, investment documentation, cap table changes and ongoing governance.

  • Partner with the business, Regulatory Legal and Regulatory Compliance teams on expansion into and launches in new markets across the UK and EMEA, including regulatory mapping, entity and licensing considerations, and corporate governance requirements.

  • Work closely with Compliance, Risk and other LRC teams globally to help align Airwallex’s policies, procedures and corporate governance frameworks across jurisdictions, with particular focus on UK requirements.

  • Draft, review and negotiate referral agreements, marketing and sponsorship agreements, and other commercial arrangements in collaboration with Partnerships, Marketing and GTM teams, ensuring risks are appropriately managed and documented.

  • Advise on legal issues related to marketing, advertising and promotions, including claims, disclosures, digital campaigns, co-marketing and referral programmes, and support review of customer-facing materials for legal and regulatory compliance.

  • Coordinate and manage outside counsel on specialised matters in the UK and across EMEA, ensuring advice is high-quality, cost-effective and aligned to Airwallex’s risk appetite and business goals.

  • Use technology and AI-enabled tools, such as templates, playbooks, contract lifecycle tools and knowledge bases, to increase the speed, consistency and quality of legal work.

Who you are

Airwallex is looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. Preferred qualifications are great to have but are not mandatory.

Minimum qualifications

You have:

  • Qualification as a solicitor or barrister in England and Wales, or an equivalent qualification in another UK jurisdiction, and are in good standing with the relevant professional body.

  • Proven experience in financial services and corporate law, preferably gained at a fast-growing technology or fintech company and/or a top-tier law firm.

  • Demonstrated interest in financial services regulation and the fintech industry, and willingness to go deep on payments, e-money, money services and related regulatory topics in the UK and EMEA.

  • In-depth knowledge of, or strong familiarity with, the UK legal and business environment, including how UK legislation, FCA requirements and cross-border rules impact fintech and payments businesses.

  • Proven experience drafting and negotiating corporate and commercial agreements, with strong written and verbal communication skills that make complex issues clear to non-lawyers.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, including Corporate Development, Finance, Product, Compliance, Risk and Marketing, across time zones.

  • Demonstrated capability in managing and leading outside counsel, including scoping work, controlling costs and consolidating advice into clear recommendations.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a practical, business-oriented approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Preferred qualifications

It would be great if you also have:

  • Experience supporting fundraising transactions, M&A or strategic investments, including due diligence and deal execution, ideally in a technology or fintech context.

  • Prior in-house experience in a fintech, payments or broader financial services company, particularly one operating across the UK and multiple EMEA jurisdictions.

  • Experience advising on legal issues related to marketing, advertising and promotions, including digital marketing, performance marketing, referral programmes and brand partnerships.

  • Exposure to UK financial services regulatory frameworks, including the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, the Payment Services Regulations 2017, the Electronic Money Regulations 2011, FCA rules and guidance, and applicable financial promotions requirements.

  • Experience partnering with Regulatory Legal, Regulatory Compliance or licensing teams on market expansion initiatives and regulatory change.

  • Comfort using technology, AI and legal operations tools to increase the speed and quality of legal work, for example playbooks, templates, contract lifecycle tools or knowledge bases.

Location

This role is based in our London office, with hybrid in-office expectations consistent with Airwallex’s local policies.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Associate Data Scientist (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.


Your Mission

As a Data Scientist at Predium, you will help develop and improve the data-driven models behind our platform. You will use statistics, machine learning, and numerical methods to solve well-defined problems related to buildings, energy performance, and real-estate decarbonization.
Working closely with our engineering and product team, you will turn real-world data into reliable analytical, simulation, and machine-learning models that identify optimization opportunities for more sustainable buildings and help customers make informed investment decisions.


What you'll own

  1. Develop and improve analytical, machine-learning, and simulation models to address business problems in the real-estate and energy domain.
  2. Build and improve data extraction pipelines for structured and unstructured sources, evaluating extraction accuracy and reliability
  3. Continuously explore and evaluate new data sources to improve model accuracy.
  4. Assess data quality, identify gaps and evaluate model performance by validating assumptions and results against real-world data and feedback of domain experts.
  5. Collaborate with data scientists, engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to translate business needs into data-driven solutions.


What success looks like

  1. You take ownership of well-defined analytical and modeling problems and independently deliver robust solutions.
  2. Your models and analyses are reproducible, well-documented, and supported by appropriate validation.
  3. You translate technical results into clear implications for the product, our customers, and the business.
  4. You collaborate effectively across Data, Engineering and Product teams.
  5. You actively seek feedback and use it to improve both your technical work and your way of working.


What it takes

  1. A degree in data science, computer science, mathematics or a related field.
  2. 1–2 years of relevant hands-on experience, with programming, ideally in Python, through projects in areas such as physics-based modeling, machine learning, or data pipelines. TypeScript experience for product prototyping is a plus.
  3. A structured, independent approach to problem-solving.
  4. Curiosity about business needs and the ability to explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  5. Confident communication in English; German is a plus.
Bonus:
  1. Initial experience with optimization methods, LLM-based data extraction, or uncertainty and sensitivity analysis.
  2. Familiarity with real estate, building physics, or energy systems.
  3. Experience with tools for physical simulation or energy modeling.


Why Predium?

  • Stage: ~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Yes, it's messy sometimes - that's the whole point. If you're looking for a job with a finished playbook, this isn't the right fit.

  • Impact: You're not cog #100 in some company. The models you build feed straight into our product and get used by real customers. Your contribution shows up directly, in revenue and in the product.

  • Ownership: We don't manage your time, we measure your results. You get responsibility and freedom - and the expectation that you'll use both.

  • Compensation: Competitive salary, bonus, and equity. We want you to share in the success you help create.

  • Team: Office-first in Munich's Werksviertel, 4 days/week.
30 vacation days (including company vacation) · Wellpass · Deutschland-Ticket · Jobrad · team events

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer (all genders)
jobs.description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Senior Network Engineer to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations (Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, Munich).


Contabo Group operates one of Europe's largest cloud infrastructure platforms, with data centres across Europe and beyond. As our new Senior Network Engineer, you take on the network backbone that thousands of customers rely on every day, with real ownership from day one.

Right now, the biggest milestone on your plate is the build out of our new AI data centre. You inherit a fully designed Leaf-Spine architecture built on Arista EOS, BGP EVPN, and VXLAN, take ownership of it, refine it where it needs refining, and drive everything from commissioning through to stable production operations. Alongside that, you keep our existing LTG infrastructure running reliably: you design, build, and operate complex network, server, and security systems, analyse and resolve faults, and harden our network security through scrubbers, firewalls, ACLs, and NAC.

You monitor network traffic and infrastructure performance, extrapolate the KPIs that matter to management, and coordinate with external service providers and remote hands across the globe. You keep our network diagrams, runbooks, change logs, and system documentation in good shape, and you work closely with Platform Engineering on Cilium BGP peering, Kubernetes node network configuration, and IPAM, acting as the ongoing interface between NetOps and Platform.

You join a self-organising, agile team that owns its problems end to end, from analysis to resolution, without micromanagement. On top of that, you will have real room to grow into infrastructure automation, DDoS mitigation with Nokia Deepfield, observability, and BGP EVPN fabric engineering, alongside plenty of national and international project work.

You report directly to our Head of Network and become the permanent owner of everything networking related at Contabo Group, Blue and Black alike. Communication, team orientation, problem solving, and analytical thinking matter just as much here as deep technical expertise, since you will regularly work across teams and explain complex topics to people outside networking.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • minimum 5 years of hands-on experience with complex, scalable networks and fabric infrastructures on Cisco and/or Arista, ideally with real Leaf-Spine and BGP EVPN VXLAN exposure
  • strong expertise in WAN connectivity, data centre peering, uplink management, VPN, and IPv6
  • strong expertise in security administration and DDoS mitigation (e.g. Nokia Deepfield, Aurologic), plus solid monitoring skills with tools like Grafana, Check_MK, or Zabbix
  • good scripting and automation skills with Ansible, Terraform, Python, or similar
  • strong analytical and strategic thinking, paired with clear, confident communication
  • a results-driven, hands-on mindset with a high standard of performance, customer orientation, and composure under pressure
  • genuine team spirit, reliability, and a self-driven way of working that thrives without micromanagement
  • experience with Network Access Control solutions, BGP Flowspec, virtualisation (Proxmox), and IPAM systems such as NetBox
  • strong conflict-handling skills, a knack for building contacts across teams, and openness to change
  • a basic understanding of Kubernetes networking, ideally paired with an Arista certification (or equivalent Cisco knowledge), a completed IT apprenticeship or equivalent, and German language skills alongside excellent English
We know that you may not currently meet all the requirements. But if you come to us with the right amount of commitment and enthusiasm, we can take off together and make a big difference.


Awesome Prospects

At Contabo, we are constantly evolving. Our growth creates space for new ideas, ownership, and real impact for people who want to make a difference.

What defines us is trust, direct communication, and an open feedback culture. We believe the best solutions are built together and that everyone has the opportunity to contribute, grow, and leave their own footprint.

  • Be part of a diverse team – Work in an international environment shaped by diversity

jobs.title: Customer Support Engineer - London
jobs.description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

As a Support Engineer at Heidi, you’ll apply deep technical expertise to diagnose, resolve, and prevent complex issues in our AI-powered healthcare product.

Your work directly impacts product reliability, customer trust, and Heidi’s ability to scale safely in high-stakes clinical environments. By owning technical issues end-to-end and partnering closely with engineering and product teams, you’ll play a critical role in supporting clinicians, improving patient care, and contributing to the long-term success of our company.

What you’ll do

  • Act as an escalation point for customers and internal team members on complex or technical issues particularly for escalated or high-impact cases.

  • Become a product expert, developing a deep understanding of how Heidi works and how customers use it in real-world clinical contexts.

  • Provide exceptional technical support by clearly understanding customer needs, communicating effectively, and resolving issues accurately and efficiently.

  • Perform in-depth analysis and debugging of complex technical issues, applying sound judgment and care in high-trust healthcare environments.

  • Own customer issues from initial contact through to resolution, ensuring timely, accurate responses within agreed service levels.

  • Collaborate closely with engineering and product teams to understand, reproduce, and resolve complex technical problems - ensuring escalations are clearly documented well-scoped, and aligned with customer impact.

  • Monitor server health, system status, and bug reports, taking immediate action to mitigate impact, escalate critical issues, and prevent recurring problems.

  • Proactively identify systemic or recurring issues and contribute to improvements across tooling, processes, and systems that increase product reliability, support efficiency, and the team’s ability to scale, including helping identify and address recurring issues.

 

What you'll need

  • 2+ years’ experience in a support engineer role.

  • A proactive individual who thrives in a fast-paced startup environment and enjoys collaborating with an international team dedicated to building impactful AI experiences.

  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to think critically and learn on the fly.

  • Strong customer focus - you excel at and genuinely enjoy helping customers.

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to question, clarify, empathise, use appropriate tone and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users in a clear, empathetic manner.

  • Understanding of web development, with some experience using Python, React, Node, FastAPI, and MongoDB.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We offer health and dental cover, a £700 annual learning and development budget, a £100/month health and wellness allowance, a £500 home office budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, four weeks of work from anywhere per year, and serious equity.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

jobs.description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.

✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. 

Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.

🏠 Contexte

Présentation du sujet

Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).

Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.

En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.

Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.

Contexte scientifique

La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.

Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.

La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.

Contexte opérationnel

Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :

  • les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;

  • les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;

  • les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;

  • les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).

Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.

Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.


🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

Démarche de la thèse

L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.

Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.

Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).

Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.

Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.

Verrous scientifiques :

  • Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)

  • Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles

  • Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies

  • Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles

Objectifs de développement durable rattachés :

ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·

ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables

ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus.

Compétences requises :

  • Méthodes qualitatives : conduite et analyse d'entretiens semi-directifs, observation de terrain, analyse de corpus documentaires.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
The product you will work on

The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. 


Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.


The ideal candidate is

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.


This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.


Your role and responsibilities

You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.


Build the platform

  • Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.

  • Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.

  • Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.

  • Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.

  • Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.

  • Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior

  • .

Run what you build

  • Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.

  • Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.

  • Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.

  • Be part of a compensated on-call rotation


Set the technical direction

  • Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.

  • Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.

  • Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.


What you need to succeed in this role

  • Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.

  • Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.

  • Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.

  • Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.

  • Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.

  • A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.

  • A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.

  • Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.

  • Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.

  • Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.

  • Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.

  • A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.

  • Experience in using AI for engineering.


Nice to haves

  • Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.

  • Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.

  • Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.

  • Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.

  • Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects


We offer you

At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme.

You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching.

jobs.title: Training Specialist (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Why should you join?

DocuWare stands for globally distributed, international teams and an open corporate culture that invites you to help shape it. Mobile Work and flexible working hours are part of our everyday life. Would you like to be part of an innovative company whose solutions are digitizing everyday work in a wide range of industries? In that case, we are happy to welcome you to the team.


Your Responsibilities

As a Training Specialist (m/f/d), you will empower our sales teams and partners to successfully sell, confidently demonstrate, and effectively implement DocuWare solutions for our customers. Leveraging your expertise, you will develop modern learning programs, deliver engaging training experiences, and play a key role in strengthening the success of our sales and partner organizations.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • You plan, coordinate, and deliver training programs for our sales teams and partners, ensuring an engaging and effective learning experience.
  • You design modern training concepts and define appropriate methodologies and instructional approaches to enable sustainable knowledge transfer.
  • You create, update, and continuously improve training programs based on business requirements and learning objectives.
  • You develop and maintain high-quality training materials, including course content, e-learning modules, assessments, and certification programs.
  • You collaborate closely with sales teams, partners, and cross-functional stakeholders to align training content with business needs and audience expectations.
  • You support the creation, maintenance, and enhancement of product demonstrations for our sales teams and partners.
  • You act as a subject matter expert in meetings, workshops, and events, providing guidance on sales and product-related topics.
  • You identify opportunities to improve existing training offerings and actively contribute new ideas to enhance our learning and enablement programs.


What you need to succeed

  • You hold a degree in Education, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or have gained equivalent qualifications through relevant professional experience.
  • You are skilled at adapting to different audiences and levels of expertise, delivering content in a clear, practical, and impactful way.
  • You have ideally gained experience in training, enablement, learning & development, or technical support.
  • You are proficient in Microsoft Office, CRM systems, and modern presentation and collaboration tools, and you are confident delivering both in-person and virtual training sessions.
  • You have a solid understanding of the customer journey, sales processes, and common sales methodologies such as SPIN.
  • You possess a strong understanding of business processes and their translation into digital workflows, and you can quickly familiarize yourself with complex software solutions.
  • Experience with DocuWare or other document management solutions is an advantage.
  • You are fluent in both German and English, with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • You work independently, thrive in international team environments, and bring strong communication, networking, and interpersonal skills.


What we can offer

There are many great reasons to join DocuWare - our company culture is only one of them.
 As part of the DocuWare team, you will benefit from many advantages:

  • Globally distributed, international teams: You will find our teams working in Germering, New York, Sofia or other worldwide locations.
  • Flexible work location and hours: You work hybrid - on the road or in our modern office - and you have the flexibility to arrange your own working hours.
  • Individual support: After an intensive induction, you will receive regular training tailored to your needs (e.g. conferences internal team building measures).
  • Well-earned rest: 35 vacation days per year, sport offerings, massages, a football table and a relaxing lounge area.
  • Mental health support: With our employee assistance program you have free and confidential access to resources and support for your well-being and stress management at any time.
  • Healthy food: Together we enjoy Fairtrade coffee with organic milk or oat milk, snacks and fresh fruit - all free of charge - as well as subsidized lunch from the Foodji fridge.
  • Free Tuesday Lunch: Every Tuesday, enjoy a complimentary and varied lunch.
  • Good accessibility: Choose how you would like to come to the office with a leased e-bike, by train or via highways A96/A99 (you can charge your e-car on site for free).
  • Team spirit: Regular employee and team events (virtual or on-site) ensure excellent collaboration with colleagues around the world.
  • Sustainability and social commitment: DocuWare stands for paperless work and supports volunteer organizations and local sports clubs.
  • Planning for your future: DocuWare subsidizes your company pension plan!
  • We offer a stable job with a well established and growing company.
  • Unique benefits: Choose one of three great options (Bonago, E-Gym or subsidized Deutschlandticket) to suit your needs.
  • We only use the latest technologies - find out more on Stackshare.
  • Up to 30 Days Work from Abroad: Experience international opportunities and broaden your horizons.
  • Family First: Preferential registration in our selected daycare center in Germering (no guarantee).
  • Buddy Program: You'll be paired with a buddy, who will support you during your onboarding and offer valuable tips.
For better insights, check us out on Instagram!
